title: Shape-morphing 4D bioprinted magnetic constructs for cartilage regeneration
author: Chakraborty, Roy, et al.

steps.title: Expand BM‑MSC culture
steps.instruction: Seed 5 × 10⁵ human BM‑MSCs in a T75 flask with expansion medium, incubate at 5 % CO₂, change medium every 2 days, and passage at 80 % confluency using trypsin‑EDTA, resuspending cells in 1 mL fresh expansion medium and counting cell density; use passages 3–6.

steps.title: Prepare expansion medium
steps.instruction: Add 50 mL fetal bovine serum (10 %) to 440 mL α‑MEM with GlutaMAX, then add 5 mL of 37.5 µg/mL L‑AA‑2‑P and 5 mL of 100 U/mL penicillin‑streptomycin; mix with a 25 mL serological pipette, aliquot into 50 mL portions, and sterile‑filter through a 0.2 µm syringe filter.

steps.title: Prepare chondrogenic medium
steps.instruction: Add 5 mL L‑AA‑2‑P to 479.45 mL DMEM/F12 with GlutaMAX, then add 5 mL ITS Liquid Media Supplement (100×) and 5 mL Proline, followed by 5 mL penicillin‑streptomycin (10 000 U/mL); mix, aliquot 49.95 mL into 50 mL conical tubes, add 5 µL TGF‑β1 freshly before use, and sterile‑filter through a 0.2 µm syringe filter.

steps.title: Degum silk cocoons
steps.instruction: Cut cocoons into dime‑sized pieces, weigh 5 g, place in a 2 L glass beaker with 1.5 L ultrapure water, bring to boil, add 4.24 g Na₂CO₃ (0.02 M) slowly, add cocoon pieces, boil 20 min while stirring occasionally, rinse fibers with cold ultrapure water, squeeze excess water with muslin cloth, discard Na₂CO₃ solution, repeat Na₂CO₃ addition and boiling once more, then wash fibers in 1 L beaker with 500–600 mL ultrapure water on a stir plate for 10–15 min, repeat 5–6 times, squeeze, spread on aluminum foil and dry overnight in a fume hood. Store dried degummed fibers at room temperature in a clean bag or wrapped in foil.

steps.title: Dissolve fibers in LiBr
steps.instruction: Prepare a 20 % (w/v) LiBr solution (9.3 M) for 5 g dried fibers: calculate 25 mL water and 20.11 g LiBr, add LiBr to ~60 % of the water on ice (exothermic), then bring to final volume; pack degummed fibers tightly into a 50 mL glass beaker, add the LiBr solution, and incubate in an oven at 60 °C for 4 h until the solution becomes amber, transparent, and fully dissolved.

steps.title: Dialyze and concentrate silk solution
steps.instruction: Hydrate dialysis cassettes, load the warm silk‑LiBr solution into a cassette using a 20 mL syringe with an 18‑gauge needle (insert a second needle for air release), and dialyze against 1 L cold ultrapure water (with ice) on a magnetic stir plate; change the water nine times over 48 h (1 h intervals three times, 2 h, evening overnight, next morning, afternoon, night, and the following morning). Remove the silk solution with a syringe, collect in 50 mL Falcon tubes (split if >40 mL), centrifuge at 9 000 rpm (~12 700 g) at 4 °C for 20 min, discard flocculent/brown matter, and determine concentration by drying 0.5 mL of solution at 60 °C in a pre‑weighed boat, weighing the dried silk and dividing by 0.5 mL to obtain % w/v (typically 4–6 %). Store the silk fibroin solution at 4 °C for up to one month.

steps.title: Synthesize Fe₂O₃ nanoparticles
steps.instruction: In a Duran bottle, dissolve 92.4 g Fe(ClO₄)₃·6H₂O, 1.3 g NaH₂PO₄·H₂O, and 12 g (NH₂)₂CO in 2 L milli‑Q water, seal and place in an oven pre‑heated to 100 °C for 24 h, then cool to room temperature; decant most supernatant, transfer sediment with residual liquid to 250 mL high‑speed centrifuge tubes, centrifuge at 10 000 rpm for 10 min, discard supernatant, redisperse pellet in fresh milli‑Q water, and repeat washing (centrifuge and resuspend) at least four times until the supernatant is clear. Transfer the washed tubes to a vacuum oven at 80 °C (unsealed) under vacuum overnight (≥16 h), cool under a fume hood, grind the dried solid to a fine powder, and store in a sealed glass vial.

steps.title: Reduce Fe₂O₃ to Fe₃O₄
steps.instruction: In a laminar‑flow hood, place the desired mass of Fe₂O₃ powder and the stoichiometric amount of TiH₂ powder into a semi‑cylindric ceramic holder, insert the holder into a quartz tube, seal both ends, connect one end to an argon flow line, purge with argon, raise furnace temperature to 250 °C under argon and hold for 5 min to remove moisture, then stop argon flow, increase temperature to 370 °C and hold for 6 h, allow the furnace to cool to room temperature, degas the tube by opening the valves, and collect the reduced black Fe₃O₄ powder, storing it in a sealed glass vial.

steps.title: Prepare control SF‑G bioink
steps.instruction: Sterilize gelatin (G) in molecular‑grade ethanol overnight in a 90 mm petri dish inside a laminar flow hood, weigh 80 mg (8 % w/v), add the sterile gelatin to 800 µL autoclaved 5 % silk fibroin (SF) solution in a 2 mL Eppendorf tube, incubate at 37 °C for 30 min in a water bath, add 100 µL 10X media supplement (filter‑sterilized) and add sterile FBS to a final concentration of 10 %, mix gently, and finally suspend 1 × 10⁷ cells mL⁻¹ to obtain the cell‑laden control bioink (SF‑G).

steps.title: Prepare magnetic SF‑G‑MNP bioink
steps.instruction: Rinse the Fe₃O₄ MNPs with deionized water 2–3 times, dry at 100 °C until completely water‑free, sterilize under UV in a 90 mm petri dish for 1 h (lid removed), ultrasonicate 5 mg MNPs in 500 µL PBS for 5 min at 50 % amplitude (20 kHz), add this suspension to the acellular control bioink, adjust the total volume to achieve 5 mg mL⁻¹ MNP concentration, and finally suspend 1 × 10⁷ cells mL⁻¹ to obtain the magnetic bioink (SF‑G‑MNP). Note: distribute gelatin along the tube wall and add the SF solution at a 45°–50° angle to avoid aggregation.
